findings.reason: Rejected. The observation is true, but the owner already exists and the proposed fix is wrong in two places. (1) No node states Shimura's bounded-denominators theorem. data/decompositions/AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights.json only imports Shimura Thm 3.52 for Serre's dimension comparison 3.1.3 ('quoted from Shimura Thm 3.52 … not in the supplied library and was not read'), and a search of all decompositions, packets and new roadmaps finds no statement of it. The other 'bounded denominator' hits are Faltings's height-difference Bemerkung (R28.2), Liouville's inequality (DT) and Kolyvagin classes (HE). Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8 cites 'Shimura Thm 3.48/3.51/3.52' only as source support for coefficient fields. (2) But it is not ownerless. PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25 has the missing item PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25/shimura-bounded-denominators, routed by its source route 6 to AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.2. Its review (PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25.review.json, commit a186b292, 23 September 2026) accepts all nine routes, including route 6. The red team quotes this very route's reason, but reads it as a record of absence; in fact it is the ownership decision. research/blueprint/make_queue.py (lines 830–839, 941) turns an accepted source route into an 'added source' in the owning roadmap's blueprint prompt ('The maintainer added these sources to this roadmap. Cover them completely … within the stages they belong to'), with the route reason and item ids. The owning blueprint, BP-AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights, is still pending in research/blueprint/queue.json (issue #671, state:available). So the next queue generation hands the R15.2 node to that blueprint job, and a fix job would duplicate it. The only real defect is procedural: the live GitHub issue #671 was last refreshed on 2026-09-23T13:30Z, before the CDT25 review merged (17:30Z), and its body does not yet contain the CDT25 source. It should be regenerated, not given a second owner. (3) The proposed statement is false as written: 'for a modular form on a finite-index subgroup whose q-expansion has algebraic coefficients, the denominators … are bounded'. For non-congruence finite-index subgroups this fails; that is exactly CDT25's theorem (the unbounded denominators conjecture: bounded denominators force congruence modularity, item thm-1.0.1). The node must be stated for congruence subgroups, as CDT25's item has it: a holomorphic form of weight k on Γ(M) with rational (more generally algebraic) Fourier coefficients at i∞ has D·f ∈ ℤ[[q^{1/M}]] for some D ≥ 1 (Shimura 1971, Theorem 3.52), with denominators bounded at primes dividing the level too, which is the point beyond R15.2's q-expansion principle over ℤ[1/n]. (4) The IntegralIwasawaTheory half of the fix is also wrong. I.3's 'distribution/bounded-denominator theorem' concerns Hilbert modular Eisenstein series. Shimura 3.52 for elliptic modular forms does not supply it, and I.3 already assigns it to itself ('must be imported from a verified supplier or implemented as the Iwasawa proof's explicit prerequisite'). Pointing I.3 at the classical node would record a supplier that does not cover its case. No fix job is warranted. The maintainer should refresh issue #671 so that the pending blueprint receives CDT25 route 6, and that blueprint should state the node for congruence subgroups as above.
